title: Travel Protection Plans: Recoveries Note on the Amount Restored to a Benefit
content:
Where a supplier has paid the traveller for a loss a Travel Protection Plans certificate has already settled, the traveller declares what they received and that amount is restored to the benefit the certificate records as consumed.

**The amount the supplier has paid.** It is taken as every amount the supplier has returned on the traveller's booking for the journey, counted as a positive amount whichever way the booking's own record carries it.

**The two shares it is taken at.** That amount is then taken at the share which the evidence standing behind it carries and at the share which the certificate takes back. The share which the evidence standing behind it carries is 70 per cent. The share which the certificate takes back is the whole of it, 100 per cent.

**The bound.** The amount the restoration is held to is the largest payment the certificate has settled less the deductible withheld from it.

**The amount restored.** It is the lesser of the amount so taken and the amount the restoration is held to, rounded to two decimal places, and it is entered against the benefit consumed as a negative figure.

## The quantity defined in order

The amount so taken is built in one pass from the amount the supplier has paid: that amount at the share the evidence standing behind it carries, and the result at the share the certificate takes back. That figure is then set beside the amount the restoration is held to, and the lesser of the two is the amount restored. The rounding to two decimal places is done on the lesser of the two, after the comparison rather than before it, and the figure is entered against the benefit consumed as a negative amount so that the benefit consumed falls by it.

## Worked to a figure on hypothetical inputs

Take a certificate on which the supplier has returned 900.00 USD in all on the traveller's booking for the journey, and which has settled one payment of 800.00 USD with 50.00 USD withheld from it as a deductible.

- The amount the supplier has paid is 900.00 USD.
- At the share the evidence standing behind it carries, 70 per cent, that is 630.00 USD.
- At the share the certificate takes back, 100 per cent, that is 630.00 USD. This is the amount so taken.
- The amount the restoration is held to is 800.00 USD less 50.00 USD, which is 750.00 USD.
- The lesser of 630.00 USD and 750.00 USD is 630.00 USD, which rounded to two decimal places is 630.00 USD.
- The amount restored is therefore entered against the benefit consumed as a negative 630.00 USD.

Had the supplier returned 1600.00 USD instead, the amount so taken would be 70 per cent of 1600.00 USD at the whole of the certificate's share, which is 1120.00 USD; the amount the restoration is held to would still be 750.00 USD, and being the lesser of the two it would be the amount restored.
